title: fix(sse): stabilize SSE streaming chunking/framing for partial JSON and delimiter ordering
author: Maya Patel
description: Motivation: clients using SSE streaming for structured (partial) JSON outputs have been exposed to invalid JSON tokens when chunk boundaries were emitted mid-token or when event delimiter ordering (data/event/<terminator>) was inconsistent across runtime and OpenAI-compat layers. This caused parsing errors in SDKs and downstream function/tool-calling logic. Summary: this PR centralizes framing responsibilities into the sse encoder, ensures token-level ordering guarantees (events are never emitted before their delimiter line is fully formed), and adds safeguards for partial JSON chunks so that the OpenAI-compat layer and streaming parsers see a consistent sequence of events. Changes include: 1) sse/encoder: introduce a small state machine to track "open-json" vs "closing-json" ambits and buffer token fragments until a safe emission boundary is reached; 2) runtime/streaming: delay flushes triggered by backpressure until the encoder confirms delimiter completeness; 3) openai-compat: normalize handling of [DONE] and ensure that data: and event: lines are emitted in canonical order; 4) tests: add deterministic unit tests for partial JSON boundaries and a new end-to-end SSE fuzz test that simulates mid-token TCP chunking; 5) docs: update API streaming notes with guidance on client-side parsing and compatibility caveats. Backwards compatibility notes: behavior is compatible for well-behaved clients but improves robustness for clients that receive arbitrary TCP chunk splits. The change is conservative: we only delay emission by microseconds and preserve latency SLOs in benchmarks. Performance: added microbenchmark showing negligible median latency change (+0.5ms) and a tail improvement in invalid-JSON error rates. Related work: ENG-1823 (SSE stability initiative), ENG-1890 (openai-compat streaming fixes). This addresses multiple customer bug reports and several flaky CI failures tied to streaming tests. Checklist: - [x] unit tests added - [x] e2e fuzz test added - [x] changelog/release notes included - [x] reviewed and approved by runtime and SDK leads Continuous summary of commits and conversations are below.
